full_judgment:
2. The facts, relevant for disposal of the instant civil petition for leave to appeal, are that Senayet Ali the predecessor of the respondents as plaintiff filed Other Class Suit No. 27 of 1979, which was subsequently renumbered several times and finally numbered as Other Class Suit No. 71 of 1994, in the Court of Assistant Judge, Ramu, Cox's Bazar, for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession in respect of the suit land described in the schedule of the plaint. The original plaintiff having died his heirs were substituted as plaintiffs in the suit. It was contended, inter alia, that one Md Jalal Ahmed obtained the suit land on 19-2-1963 by a settlement under khatian No. 1247/418 of Jhilenza Mouza vide Settlement Case No. 156/1961-62 and, thereafter, on 10-3-1967 he sold out the said land in favour of Senayet Ali by two registered deeds. Senayet Ali possessed the land by paying rent through one Sultan Ahmed and Syedullah. He took half share of the land by kabala in the name of the defendant No. 10, who had no right, title, interest or possession of the land. Defendant No. 7 also obtained settlement by the same settlement case from Jalal Ahmed and got 0.50 decimals of land to the contiguous east of the suit land. Defendant No. 7 subsequently sold out the same in favour of one Moulvi Emdadul Hoq and others. The defendants in the absence of the plaintiffs in the first part of 1997 trespassed into the suit land and upon dispossessing the plaintiffs, constructed 4 huts therein. They also ignored the request of the plaintiffs' caretaker as well as the plaintiffs' request to vacate the premises. The defendants also in collusion with the settlement officials recorded their names in the BS khatian which constrained the plaintiffs' predecessor to file the suit. 

 3. Defendant Nos. 1 and 4-6 contested the suit by filing written statement contending, inter alia, that defendant Nos. 7 and 8 obtained settlement of 50 decimals of 'nul' land in settlement khatian No. 8105/2 which is adjacent west of the suit land. Jalal Ahmed obtained settlement of 40 decimals of hilly land and the remaining 30 decimals of land of suit plot remained as khas. The MRR khatian No. 8105/9289 was recorded in the name of the defendant No. 7. Defendant No. 7 thereafter by two sets of deeds dated 26-4-1976 and 28-4-1976 sold 14 decimals of land to defendant No. 4 and by another kabala dated 26-8-1977 defendant No. 7 sold to defendant No. 1. After acquiring the land by purchase, these defendants have been possessing the suit land by constructing their dwelling house and filling earth. The case of contesting defendant No. 32 is that by Settlement Case No. 156/1961-62 this defendant obtained 50 decimals of land and accordingly the MRR and BS khatian were recorded. This defendant by kabala dated 26-8-1977 purchased 10 decimals of land from the suit land and, thereafter, by filling earth converted the 'nul' land to 'bhiti' and by constructing dwelling house is possessing the same. The plaintiffs having no right, title, interest and possession in the suit land filed the suit on false allegation. 

 6. Mr Abdus Sobhan, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner submitted that the High Court Division failed to consider that the suit is for recovery of khas possession and admittedly the plaintiffs did not mention the boundary of the suit land in the schedule of the plaint and thus the Courts below as well as the High Court Division could not determine the actual quantum of dispossessed land in suit, and as such the impugned judgement and order is liable to be set aside.
